## Purpose and top-level entry points
GDevelop is a no-code game-development system: a React/Electron/browser editor authors event-driven game projects; C++ core models and transforms them; JavaScript/TypeScript runtime executes exported games. Primary entry points are the editor bootstrap at `newIDE/app/src/index.js`, desktop host at `newIDE/electron-app/app/main.js`, runtime game shell at `GDJS/Runtime/index.html`, and CMake workspace at `CMakeLists.txt`.

## Canonical project model and persistence
`Core/GDCore/Project` is the engine-independent in-memory model for projects: scenes/layouts, objects, instances, behaviors, variables, resources, effects, and event-based entities. `Project` is the aggregate boundary; serializers translate this graph to persisted project data, including JSON via embedded RapidJSON. Editor and exporters should manipulate this model rather than duplicate project semantics.
Paths: `Core/GDCore/Project/Project.h`, `Core/GDCore/Project/Layout.h`, `Core/GDCore/Serialization/Serializer.cpp`.

## Event language, validation, and generation
The event system represents conditions/actions, control-flow events, and expressions as structured AST-like objects. Parsers and IDE analyzers validate, search, refactor, autocomplete, and resolve dependencies against extension metadata. Code generators then emit target-specific event code with diagnostics and scoped generation context.
Paths: `Core/GDCore/Events/EventsList.h`, `Core/GDCore/Events/Parsers/ExpressionParser2.cpp`, `Core/GDCore/Events/CodeGeneration/EventsCodeGenerator.cpp`.

## Extension and platform contract
Extensions declare object types, behaviors, instructions, expressions, effects, dependencies, and parameter metadata. Core built-ins supply common engine concepts; `GDJS` provides a JavaScript platform’s corresponding metadata/code generation; `Extensions` adds packaged feature implementations. This metadata boundary allows the editor to construct UI and validate project content without hard-coding every feature.
Paths: `Core/GDCore/Extensions/Metadata/MetadataProvider.h`, `Core/GDCore/Extensions/Builtin/AllBuiltinExtensions.h`, `GDJS/GDJS/Extensions/JsPlatform.cpp`.

## JavaScript export pipeline and runtime
The JS platform exporter converts the Core project/event graph into game JavaScript and packaged resources. At runtime, `RuntimeGame` owns game lifecycle and scenes; `RuntimeScene` owns per-scene objects/layers/events; resource managers load and cache assets. Generated events invoke runtime APIs and extension runtime implementations.
Paths: `GDJS/GDJS/IDE/Exporter.cpp`, `GDJS/GDJS/Events/CodeGeneration/EventsCodeGenerator.cpp`, `GDJS/Runtime/runtimegame.ts`.

## Rendering and execution targets
The runtime is TypeScript/JavaScript and primarily renders 2D through PixiJS, with Three.js integration for 3D. Platform wrappers package the same runtime for Electron, Cordova/mobile, Facebook Instant Games, or web. WebAssembly-backed extensions provide specialized physics/pathfinding capabilities.
Paths: `GDJS/Runtime/pixi-renderers/runtimegame-pixi-renderer.ts`, `GDJS/Runtime/pixi-renderers/three.js`, `GDJS/Runtime/Electron/main.js`.

## Editor application and Core bridge
`newIDE/app` is the authoring UI, centered on `MainFrame` orchestration and specialized scene, events, object, resource, and export surfaces. It consumes Core/GDJS through `GDevelop.js`, an Emscripten/WebAssembly binding layer that exposes C++ project structures and generators to browser JavaScript. Desktop-only operations are delegated from the renderer to Electron services for filesystem access, preview windows, debugging, and local processes.
Paths: `newIDE/app/src/MainFrame/index.js`, `newIDE/app/src/EventsSheet/index.js`, `GDevelop.js/Bindings/Bindings.idl`.

## Storage, services, preview, and publishing
Projects can be opened/saved through local, cloud, download, and URL storage providers. Export/preview flows select browser or local implementations and can call online build/publish services. The editor’s service client layer covers authentication, assets, builds, games, AI generation, analytics, and marketplace interactions; these are external HTTP/service boundaries, not part of Core runtime execution.
Paths: `newIDE/app/src/ProjectsStorage/ProjectStorageProviders.js`, `newIDE/app/src/ExportAndShare/BrowserExporters/index.js`, `newIDE/app/src/Utils/GDevelopServices/ApiConfigs.js`.
